title: You don’t trust God as much as you say you do.
paragraphs: You don’t trust God as much as you say you do.
Because something in you just flinched.

You post the verse.
You say “Amen.”
You lift your hands in worship.

But when life stops making sense…
you start taking control back.
And now you’re stuck between two worlds.

You believe in God…
but you don’t trust Him with this.

That situation.
That delay.
That unanswered prayer.
That pain you don’t talk about.
It’s not confusion that’s eating you alive.

You want God’s promises…
but on your timeline.

You want His blessings…
but without surrender.
So you smile on the outside.

“God, if You’re really good… why this?”
“Why now?”
“Why me?”
You don’t say it out loud.

“I trust You, Lord…
as long as I understand You.”
And Scripture cuts deeper than our comfort.

“Trust in the Lord with all your heart,
and lean not on your own understanding;
in all your ways acknowledge Him,
and He shall direct your paths.”
It’s limited to what you see.
Some scholars interpret this passage as a call to full surrender—not passive waiting, but active trust that refuses to let human logic override divine wisdom.
And that’s where it gets uncomfortable.
Because trusting God means releasing control.
And releasing control feels like dying.
But maybe that’s exactly the point.
Because the root issue isn’t confusion.
The same ancient whisper from the garden:
“You can decide what’s best for you.”
In your need to figure everything out.
And it’s been separating you from deep intimacy with God.
God didn’t wait for you to figure everything out.
Jesus Christ entered a world that didn’t understand Him.
He lived a life that didn’t make sense to human logic.
A King… born in a manger.
A Savior… rejected by His own people.
A Healer… crucified like a criminal.
Nothing about the cross looked reasonable.

Yet it was there—
in the place of greatest confusion—
that God revealed His greatest clarity.

“But God demonstrates His own love toward us,
in that while we were still sinners,
Christ died for us.”
Jesus didn’t die for your understanding.

Proving that what looks like the end…
can be the beginning.

What looks like loss…
can be resurrection.

What looks like silence…
can be God writing something eternal.
“Do you understand what God is doing?”

Will you trust Him with the relationship?
With the delay?
With the uncertainty?
With the pain you can’t explain?
Or will you keep holding on…
God is not asking you to have all the answers.
He’s asking you to lay down your need for them.
Because trust is not built on explanations.
It’s built on who He is.
Even when life doesn’t feel like it.

“Lord… I don’t understand.
But I trust You.”
Because on the other side of surrender…

“Do not be anxious about anything,
but in everything by prayer and supplication,
with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God;
and the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding,
will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.”

So stop waiting for clarity
before you obey.

Stop demanding answers
before you surrender.
And watch Him lead you into light.
If this is hitting you deep…
who’s silently struggling to trust God right now.

this might be the reminder
that pulls them back to Him.
If this stirred something in you…

From confusion to purpose.
From control to surrender.
From doubt to faith.
